raw_response:
The plot illustrates the relationship between co-occurrence number and accuracy (ACC) percentage for six different methods: Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME. The x-axis, labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” is logarithmically scaled and ranges from 0 to approximately 10^4, with major tick marks at 10^0, 10^1, 10^2, 10^3, and 10^4. The y-axis, labeled “ACC (%)”, is linearly scaled from 40% to 65%, with major tick marks at 40, 45, 50, 55, 60, and 65. The “Base” method (black solid line with circular markers) starts at approximately 38% ACC at co-occurrence number 1 and rises slightly to about 44% at 10^4. The “FT” method (blue solid line with downward-pointing triangular markers) begins at 40% and increases to about 48% at 10^4. The “IKE” method (red solid line with upward-pointing triangular markers) starts at 43% and rises to approximately 49.5% at 10^4. The “MEND” method (brown solid line with diamond markers) begins at 44% and increases to about 56.5% at 10^4. The “MEMIT” method (purple solid line with pentagonal markers) starts at 44% and rises to approximately 55% at 10^4. The “ROME” method (green solid line with square markers) begins at 51% and steadily increases to about 66% at 10^4. All lines show a generally increasing trend with increasing co-occurrence number, with ROME consistently achieving the highest ACC across the range.
